steps.en: What you see: A linear mobile flap divides the aortic lumen into true and false channels. The flap is seen in long and short axis with colour flow in both lumens and delayed sluggish flow in the false one. Root involvement gives central aortic regurgitation and pericardial blood. Any dissection involving the ascending aorta is type A and a surgical emergency, while disease confined beyond the left subclavian artery is type B.

Normal values with units: Aortic root diameter. Normal sinuses about 34 mm. Above 40 mm the root is dilated and dissection risk rises, especially with a bicuspid valve or family aortopathy.. Source: ASE 2015 chamber quantification guideline, section on aortic measurements

Blood pressure control target. Keep systolic pressure around 100 to 120 mmHg with heart rate control while arranging definitive care, avoiding delays for titration.. Source: ACEP emergency ultrasound guidance and international POCUS consensus, section on focused cardiac views

Dissection classification. Any ascending involvement is type A and surgical. Disease confined beyond the left subclavian artery is type B and usually medical unless complicated.. Source: ASE and SCA 2013 transoesophageal examination guideline, section on aortic assessment

ECG and heart sound correlation ecg: Most patients show non specific changes. Chronic hypertension leaves hypertrophy on the tracing. ST changes warn that a coronary ostium is involved, usually the right one.

ECG and heart sound correlation sounds: An early diastolic murmur marks prolapse of the valve with root involvement. Muffled sounds with shock warn of pericardial rupture blood. A pulse deficit with branch vessel involvement is found on bedside examination, not on echo.

spot.en: Landmarks: Aortic root with sinuses and sinotubular junction
Arch branches: brachiocephalic, carotid and subclavian
Left subclavian origin marking the type A and B boundary
What to report: Flap extent from root to abdomen with entry tear position if seen
Type A against type B with the left subclavian landmark stated
Regurgitation grade, effusion size and branch vessel flow
Blood pressures in both arms with pulse deficits and pain onset time
Red flags needing urgent referral: Any type A dissection, needs immediate cardiothoracic surgery with no delay for extra tests
Pericardial blood with tamponade physiology, needs immediate surgical review and not needle drainage alone
Limb ischaemia, stroke, gut pain or no urine output with type B disease, needs urgent complicated dissection care
Pitfalls: Pain can migrate as the flap extends, so re examine pulses and pressures through the stay.
Intramural haematoma and penetrating ulcer mimic dissection without a visible flap, so escalate on wall thickness alone.
Marfan, bicuspid valve and treated hypertension cluster in young Indian patients with chest pain, so ask directly.

todo.en: How to get it on the probe, step by step: Start parasternal long axis and assess root diameter, flap presence and regurgitation.
Move suprasternal and follow the arch from valve to descending aorta with colour.
Confirm the flap in two orthogonal planes with flow in both lumens.
Check the pericardial sac for blood and the descending aorta for rupture signs.
Record blood pressure in both arms and pulse status in carotids, arms and legs.

Common mistakes and how to correct them: Calling linear reverberation artefact a flap. Fix: Confirm flow on both sides with different timing and a visible entry tear. Reverberation shows no flow and vanishes with angle change.
Missing a short root flap on a dilated root. Fix: Use M mode through the wall. A true flap moves independently while the whole wall moves together.
Delaying definitive imaging for a complete surface study. Fix: Never let a surface study delay computed tomography when suspicion is high, since surface views miss the abdomen.

remember.en: Trigger immediate surgical referral for type A and complicated type B disease.

q.en: What defines a type A dissection?

o.en: Disease only in the leg arteries
A normal root with a murmur

why.en: Any ascending involvement is type A and a surgical emergency regardless of where pain is felt.

q.en: What separates a true flap from artefact?

o.en: A reverberation line with no flow
A mobile line with flow on both sides and delayed false lumen flow

why.en: True flaps divide flow into two timed channels with a visible entry tear, while artefacts show no flow.

q.en: Type A dissection is confirmed with a dilated root and regurgitation. What next?

why.en: Type A disease kills by rupture and tamponade within hours, so immediate surgery is the only pathway.

q.en: Which echo finding with shock changes the airway and access plan?

why.en: Rupture blood in the sac with tamponade physiology needs the operating room, and blind needle drainage can worsen the tear.

q.en: Which root size flags dilatation and rising risk?

why.en: Normal sinuses measure about 34 mm, so above 40 mm is dilated and prompts aortopathy review.
